paragraphs: The Z4 3.0i and 3.0si were the flagship straight-six models of the E85 roadster and E86 coupe generations, produced from 2002 to 2008. The 3.0i (2002–2006) uses the M54B30 — a 3.0-litre naturally aspirated straight-six that also powered the E46 330i and E39 530i. The 3.0si (2006–2008) uses the N52B30 — BMW's first magnesium-aluminium composite engine, lighter and more powerful than the M54, producing 261bhp compared to the earlier car's 228bhp. Knowing which one your car has matters because the engines are mechanically different — which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: The Z4 3.0i  3.0si is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre straight-six petrol fitted to the Z4 3.0i from 2002 to 2006, and widely used across the BMW range of that era. No widely-reported engine issue for this application — we still recommend a full inspection before any long journey.

The 3.0-litre straight-six petrol fitted to the Z4 3.0si from 2006 to 2008. BMW's first mass-production magnesium-aluminium engine, with notable power and efficiency improvements over the M54. No widely-reported engine issue for this application — we service it to the same standard as the M54.
